breath_title: Take care of the whole learner.
breath_text: Nearly 1 in 3 trainees at one big academic center screened food insecure, with interns hit hardest. Elsewhere this week: a 90-minute workshop that makes students more confident teachers, a review showing we barely teach how to say "I'm not sure," and new Academic Pediatrics pieces on handover and source-grounded AI at the bedside.

coffee.title: Coffee break with Beth
coffee.note: In my own words. Written by Beth, not AI.
paragraphs: The food insecurity study from Yale is somewhat staggering. Even with a low-ish survey response rate (28%), finding over 30% of trainees to have food insecurity is wild. They had 17 peds trainees (25% met criteria for food insecurity). They say that there may have been selection bias and also location cost of living impacts — but an earlier multi site study with higher participation rate still found 14% amongst trainees. Seems like meals at educational conferences might be more than a nice-to-have incentive for many …

top.headline: Almost 1 in 3 trainees screened food insecure, and interns had it worst
bullets: Anonymous survey at Yale New Haven: 164 residents and fellows (about 28% of ~600 eligible) completed the 10-item USDA module.
30.5% were food insecure; PGY-1s 45.3% vs 23.4% of later years (OR 2.71).
Lack of money was strongly tied to food insecurity (75% vs 4%); lack of time was not.
top.tip: add a validated food-security screen to your intern check-ins, and treat conference meals and move-in support as real resources, not perks.
top.citation: Mahan E, Demiray A, Huot SJ, Criscione J, Vazquez M. JAMA Netw Open. 2026;9(10):e2640774. Published online Oct 26, 2026. doi:10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2026.40774

top.headline: A 90-minute microteaching workshop builds confident near-peer teachers
bullets: IM clerkship students gave a 5-minute talk with feedback in week 1, then a revised talk in the final week.
Vs peers at other Harvard sites (41/51 vs 21/103 responded), confidence teaching rose more (beta 0.72) and so did confidence giving peer feedback (beta 0.77).
Now part of the IM clerkship and residency program; can run virtually.
top.tip: borrow the format for intern orientation: one short talk, peer feedback, and a redo at the end of the block.
top.citation: Zhou JC, Krupat E, Gottlieb BR, Kumar NL, Petersen EM, Osman NY. Acad Med. Online Oct 29, 2026. doi:10.1093/acamed/wvag343

top.headline: We barely teach how to say "I'm not sure": a scoping review
bullets: 18,810 records screened; only 21 studies made the cut, mostly UME/GME and mostly about diagnostic uncertainty.
Methods were experiential (simulation, SPs, OSCEs, role-play); fewer than half involved patients.
Mean MERSQI 10.4, and no study measured clinical practice or patient outcomes.
top.tip: a wide-open scholarship gap. Add an uncertainty-talk station to your next family-centered rounds sim and measure it.
top.citation: Papanagnou D, Dahm MR, Adamczyk A, et al., Santhosh L. Acad Med (scoping review). Online Oct 28, 2026. doi:10.1093/acamed/wvag342

quick.text: Wristbands as assessors? Physiologic signals from 152 learners in 470 sims classified faculty-rated novice vs competent with 84-85% balanced accuracy (Teye-Lartey SP et al. Adv Health Sci Educ. Online Oct 29, 2026).

Ask about the past, not hypotheticals. Past-behavior MMI questions beat situational ones (corrected r 0.44) and predicted 2 years of MSF; the professionalism station did not (Yoshimura H, Ponnamperuma G. Med Teach. Online Oct 29, 2026).

What inclusive educators do. URiM and LGBTQ+ students named educators who model compassionate care, address bias, and recognize extra burdens (Calles I, Schreiber J, Diller D. Med Teach. Online Oct 29, 2026).
Professionalism is institutional, too. Hafferty and Hamstra argue the movement should shift from individual physicians to the profession and its institutions (Acad Med. Online Oct 28, 2026).
